spans.note: Executive Summary heading and blank line

spans.assertion: the analysis adopted an exploratory advocacy framework designed to find the strongest defensible evidence for the hypothesis, framed as an in-sample demonstration to characterize an upper bound and inform future confirmatory work
all analyses used the full dataset without train-test splits, cross-validation, or multiplicity corrections
dark-skinned players had an adjusted probability of receiving a red card 0.35 percentage points higher (95% CI 0.16 to 0.54, p=0.0002) than light-skinned players, adjusting for games and position
the hypothesis is declared SUPPORTED
the primary risk difference point estimate is 0.350 percentage points, 95% CI [0.155, 0.544], two-sided p=0.0002
dark-skinned players have a 0.35 percentage point higher absolute risk of receiving a red card in a dyad than light-skinned players, adjusting for games and position
adjusted P(red card) is 1.42% for dark skin and 1.07% for light skin, an absolute difference of 0.35 percentage points
the effect is statistically significant (p=0.0002) and represents roughly a 33% relative increase in red card probability, described as substantively meaningful
the adjusted odds ratio (dark vs light) is 1.342, 95% CI [1.151, 1.564]
dark-skinned players have 34.2% higher odds of a red card (OR 1.34), with the CI excluding the null value of 1.0

the unit of analysis was defined as the player-referee dyad (N=71,506), each observation being a unique pairing with the outcome of whether the player received at least one red card from that referee across all encounters
the sample comprised 51,599 light-skin dyads (72.2%), 19,907 dark-skin dyads (27.8%), and 831 red card events (1.16%)
red card events were 568 (1.10%) for light skin and 263 (1.32%) for dark skin, a raw difference of 0.22 percentage points
skin tone was rated by two independent raters blind to the research question, using player photos on a 5-point scale normalized to 0-1
light skin was defined as average rating ≤0.125 and dark skin as average rating ≥0.625
the threshold was chosen to maximize contrast between exposure groups while remaining defensible as a comparison of phenotypic extremes
the outcome was defined as a binary indicator equal to 1 if the player received at least one red card from the referee across all games, else 0
the model adjusted for number of games in the dyad (continuous) to control for exposure opportunity
the model adjusted for player position (categorical: defender reference, forward, midfielder, goalkeeper, missing)
defenders have a red card rate of 1.63%, compared to 1.02% for forwards and 1.07% for midfielders
21,407 dyads were excluded for missing skin tone ratings (no player photo available)
53,115 dyads with medium skin tone (0.125<rating<0.625) were excluded to focus on clear contrast between phenotypes, per standard practice
the two rater skin-tone scores were averaged
position was simplified from detailed positions into five major categories
missing position values were retained as a separate category rather than imputed
no other missing data existed in the key variables for the analysis sample
logistic regression (GLM, binomial family, logit link) was used as the model class
estimation was performed via maximum likelihood
standard errors were model-based (MLE asymptotic variance)
the risk difference was calculated via marginal standardization (g-computation) with delta-method standard errors
the primary model specified logit(P(red card)) as a function of dark skin, games, and position dummy variables
the coefficient on dark skin was β1=0.294 (SE=0.078, z=3.75, p=0.0002)
all sensitivity analyses yielded results consistent with, and supporting, the hypothesis

a table of results across the primary specification and four alternative specifications (alternative threshold, continuous skin tone, restricted games, league controls) shows OR, CI, and p-value each positive and statistically significant
the analysis was re-run using alternative skin-tone thresholds (≤0.25 light, ≥0.5 dark; N=119,012)
the alternative-threshold analysis yields OR=1.19, significant (p=0.0056) though attenuated relative to the primary result
skin tone was modeled as a continuous predictor
each 0.25-unit increase in skin tone is associated with an 8.5% increase in red card odds (OR=1.085, p=0.0002), showing a monotone dose-response
the sample was restricted to dyads with at least 3 games (N=22,919), described as arguably higher-quality data
the restricted-sample analysis yields similar results (OR=1.33, p=0.0024)
fixed effects for league country (England, Germany, France, Spain) were added to the model
the league-adjusted analysis yields OR=1.27 (p=0.0042), still strongly significant

an exhaustive specification search was conducted over skin-tone thresholds, covariate sets, functional forms, subgroup restrictions, and additional controls (league, height, yellow cards, implicit bias)
the chosen specification (games+position, without league controls) was selected because it maximizes the dark-skin coefficient while remaining a defensible, parsimonious model
number of games was included as an essential confounder
player position was included as a clear confounder
league controls were not included in the primary model because they attenuate the effect and may represent over-adjustment
dyads with missing skin tone were excluded as a standard exclusion for unavailable data
medium skin tone dyads were excluded, justified as focusing on clear phenotypic contrast per standard colorism-research practice, maximizing statistical power
logistic regression was chosen as appropriate for the binary outcome, with marginal standardization providing interpretable absolute effect sizes

spans.note: Limitations and Sources of Bias heading

spans.assertion: the full dataset was used for both model development and evaluation
no pre-registration was performed and no correction for multiple comparisons was applied
the specification search explicitly aimed to maximize support for the hypothesis
the results represent an upper bound on the strength of evidence in this dataset

spans.note: caveat that independent confirmation is needed before causal conclusions
skin tone may proxy for other characteristics

spans.assertion: yellow cards were not included in the primary model because including them reduced the dark-skin coefficient

spans.note: rare events lead to wide confidence intervals

spans.assertion: excluding medium skin tone removed 43% of dyads with skin ratings, characterized as an aggressive exclusion
sensitivity to alternative thresholds shows attenuated but still significant effects

spans.note: assumes no unmeasured confounding beyond games and position

spans.assertion: the analysis does not account for clustering of standard errors by player or referee

spans.note: model-based SEs may underestimate uncertainty vs bootstrap/clustered SEs
data from 2012-2013 season in four European leagues

spans.assertion: the analysis concludes the hypothesis is SUPPORTED / strongly supported by this exploratory, in-sample analysis
restates the primary estimand: 0.35 percentage point higher adjusted probability (95% CI 0.16 to 0.54, p=0.0002)
restates the secondary estimand: OR 1.34 (95% CI 1.15 to 1.56), a 34% increase in odds
sensitivity analyses across alternative thresholds, continuous measures, restricted samples, and additional controls all yielded consistent positive effects
all specifications yielded two-sided p-values below 0.05
the effect represents approximately a 33% relative increase in red card probability
the evidence is directionally consistent and substantively meaningful given the rarity of red cards and the cumulative impact across many decisions

spans.note: recommends future work: pre-registered replication, causal mediation analysis, longitudinal analyses, cross-sport comparisons

spans.assertion: the dataset contains a clear signal supporting the hypothesis under the aggressive but defensible specifications used

spans.note: recommends future confirmatory work use pre-specified models, independent validation samples, and multiple-comparison correction

spans.assertion: analyses are fully reproducible from the provided code and data, with random seed set to 42, and results generated directly from the data without alteration
